name: Git CLI quick-start demo
description: A safe, self-contained walkthrough: create a temp project, make a file, and put it under version control with git. Everything happens in a temp folder and is cleaned up at the end.

steps.text: Git quick-start, from the command line
In this short demo we create a project and put it under version control using git.

steps.command: $demo = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'demo-recorder-sample'; if (Test-Path $demo) { Remove-Item $demo -Recurse -Force }; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $demo | Out-Null; Set-Location $demo; "Working in $demo"
steps.caption: Create a clean temp project folder
steps.say: First, a clean working folder in the temp directory.

steps.command: Set-Content -Path readme.md -Value "# Demo Project`nCreated by the demo recorder."; Get-Content readme.md
steps.caption: Create and show a README
steps.say: Now we add a small README file.

steps.command: git -c user.name='Demo User' -c user.email='demo@example.com' commit -m 'Initial commit'
steps.caption: Make the first commit
steps.say: And commit it as the first version.

steps.text: That's the git quick-start. Thanks for watching!
